election._note: By law no later than 22 August 2027 (current term runs to 23 July 2027); Wikipedia 'Next Spanish general election'. Per-constituency 3% threshold approximated as national — see docs/electoral-systems.md.

dissolution._note: Art. 115: the PM may propose dissolution to the King on the Council of Ministers' exclusive responsibility. Barred while a censure motion is pending, and no second dissolution within a year of the previous one (Art. 115.3). ICL/servat.unibe.ch, Spanish Constitution text.

upper._note: Senado, 265 seats, of which 208 are elected four per province regardless of population and 57 designated by the autonomous communities -- the most rurally over-represented chamber on the roster after Switzerland's. Art. 90: the Senate may veto a bill by absolute majority, and the Congress overrides immediately by absolute majority or after two months by a simple one, so an ordinary bill is delayed. Art. 167: a constitutional revision needs three fifths of EACH chamber. Constitucion Espanola, Arts. 69, 90 and 167.

amendment._note: Art. 167: an ordinary amendment needs a 3/5 majority in both the Congress and the Senate (or 2/3 of Congress plus 3/5 of Senate via a joint committee if they first disagree). Only Art. 168's rare total-revision path -- affecting the fundamental-rights title, requiring 2/3, a dissolution, and a referendum -- needs a stricter bar, and no amendment content in this game invokes it. ICL/servat.unibe.ch, Spanish Constitution text.
amendment._referendum_note: Art. 167: once the 3/5 revision has passed, a referendum is held if one tenth of the members of either chamber ask for it within fifteen days. Modelled as the head of state's own choice, since this game has no back-bench petition. ICL/servat.unibe.ch, Spanish Constitution text.
amendment._permits_system_change_note: No amendment content in this game targets Spain's form of state, but nothing in Title X excludes it from Art. 167's ordinary path either -- unlike Art. 168's stricter total-revision path, not modelled here. See docs/transition-model.md's named deferral.

judicial._note: Tribunal Constitucional. Art. 161(1)(a): hears the recurso de inconstitucionalidad against statutes and acts having the force of law. Constitucion Espanola, Art. 161.

formation._note: Investiture requires an absolute majority in the first round, a simple majority 48 hours later. No confidence is constructive and requires an absolute majority. Arts. 99 and 113 of the 1978 Constitution.

government._pretender_note: Whom data/laws/amendments.json's Restoration Act puts on the throne. Authored per nation because the law is generic and the dynasty is not; a monarchy points this at its own sitting monarch.

fiscal._note: General government, IMF/OECD estimates ~2023-2024, rounded. V1.2a starting policy, derived from France's anchor (see FRA.json): VAT 21% is Spain's own statutory standard rate (Tax Foundation, 'VAT Rates in Europe 2024'). Income and corporate are France's 20/25 scaled by Spain's OECD Revenue Statistics personal/corporate tax-to-GDP share against France's -- Spain leans noticeably less on personal income tax, hence 15/25. Spending is France's split scaled by general government expenditure of 45.5% of GDP against France's 57.3% (TheGlobalEconomy.com / OECD Government at a Glance 2025).
